working_title: StyleForge: Counterfactual Style Injection for Non-Generic Anime
primary_user: Solo generative media artists creating anime-style short films
painful_workflow: They want to produce high-quality anime with unique, personal art styles, but the default model outputs look generic. To achieve a distinctive aesthetic, they must manually post-process frames or write extremely complex single-prompt style descriptions that still drift.
current_workaround: Artists spend hours in Photoshop drawing over individual frames to impose their line-art or color-choice preferences. Others paste 500-word style prompts into the generator, hoping three adjectives survive, then accept the generic output and pretend the 'muted, desaturated cel-shading with weighted ink contours at 45-degree hatching' was intentional.
core_computation: GPT-5.6 analyzes the artist's reference pack (character sheets, background art, color scripts) and constructs a causal DAG linking style attributes to visual outcomes. Codex then implements an estimation engine that, for each generated frame, computes a style-propensity score by matching observed features against the reference set. For any frame flagged as 'generic' (low estimated treatment effect from the style reference), the system formulates a counterfactual: what would this frame look like if the style treatment had been fully applied? GPT-5.6 generates a targeted inpainting or control signal prompt correction via the fal API—adjusting only the deviating attributes (e.g., 'thicken line weight by estimated delta of 1.4x')—and re-submits the frame for targeted regeneration. This avoids full re-generation and converges toward the style with fewer API calls.
last_mile_action: The artist drags their style reference folder (3-10 images) onto the interface. They paste their base scene prompt and click 'Generate with Style Treatment.' A side-by-side viewer shows pairs of frames: the generic 'control' output on the left, the style-treated output on the right. Below each pair, a causal-style report reads 'Line weight confidence: 92% match to reference (up from 43%), color saturation delta applied: -22%.' The artist can adjust sliders to manually weight specific style attributes (line weight, palette adherence, shading gradient) and the counterfactual engine re-calculates treatment effects in real-time, selectively regenerating only the adjusted attributes.
visible_transformation: A flat, generic anime clip of a samurai in a forest becomes visually indistinguishable from the artist's personal sketchbook style—heavy ink contours, a restricted palette of ochre-vermillion-teal, and stylized leaf silhouettes—without the artist ever opening Photoshop or guessing at prompt engineering.

Then they switch to StyleForge, drag the same reference folder, paste the identical prompt, and click 'Generate with Style Treatment.' The tool shows a cascading estimate: 'Estimated style adherence: 37% on control frame.' A progress bar appears as Codex iterates counterfactual corrections. Within a minute, the treated frame appears side-by-side: visible ink lines now mimic the artist's brush weight, the colors match the restricted palette, and the leaf shapes echo the background key.
